candidate.title: CIRS-Seq
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina CIRS-Seq schematic, interpreted through Incarnato et al.'s 2014 native-deproteinized-RNA implementation described for mouse embryonic stem cells. Protein-associated folded RNA undergoes proteinase K treatment, then two independent chemical-probing lanes (upper interpreted as CMCT; lower labeled DMS), reverse transcription and RNA hydrolysis to yield cDNA. The leftmost titled hairpin is a method icon. The represented library precursor is stop-terminated cDNA: primary text reports downstream adapter ligation and sequencing to infer RNA accessibility. Adapter ligation, sequencing, an untreated background control and specific downstream analysis are not drawn operations. The related 2OMe-seq adaptation is outside this schematic's targets.

states.label: Protein-associated folded RNA
features: Purple RNA stem-loop is associated with a blue protein oval.
Caption In vivo folded RNA denotes the starting folding context; chemical probing occurs after protein removal.
In the primary implementation, proteinase K acts on RNA in a cell lysate; cell lysis is reported preparation history rather than an additional operation drawn here.

operations.label: Proteinase K treatment
operations.description: Remove proteins from protein-associated folded RNA, exposing RNA regions while retaining the depicted stem-loop. Proteinase K is a treatment reagent rather than a sequenced material.
operations.mechanism: Proteolysis of RNA-associated proteins after cell lysis, as reported for CIRS-seq.
operations.information_effect: Establishes native deproteinized RNA as the probed substrate. The assay therefore reports accessibility after protein removal, with the paper asserting preservation of native folding.

evidence.locator: Left-center: arrow captioned Proteinase K treatment, between protein-associated hairpin and bare RNA hairpin
[b00018], Results: native deproteinized RNA probing
evidence.quote: To perform transcriptome-wide probing of RNAs in their native deproteinized conformation, we lysed mouse ESCs in an isotonic buffer, and treated the lysate with Proteinase K to unmask regions of RNAs bound by proteins, without affecting the RNA structure (supplementary Materials and methods in Additional file 1).

operations.label: Reaction
operations.description: Upper reaction lane: introduce the depicted red/yellow ring-shaped loop modification into deproteinized RNA. This lane is interpreted as CMCT from the primary CIRS-seq dual-reagent design and the lower lane's explicit DMS label; the upper reagent name itself is absent from both supplied schematics.
operations.mechanism: For the interpreted CMCT lane, the primary paper reports adduct formation at N1 and N3 of pseudouridine, N3 of uridine and, to a lesser extent, N1 of guanosine and inosine when unpaired. The generic ring icon does not specify an adduct structure.
operations.information_effect: Encodes reagent-specific RNA accessibility as a chemical mark on the template. Positional reactivity supports inference of unpaired residues in native deproteinized RNA; it does not directly give base-pairing partners or make every low-signal residue proof of pairing.

method_scopes.rationale: CIRS-Seq, expanded in the figure as chemical inference of RNA structures, is the sole schematic target. The matching collection heading and caption confirm that scope. All seven local operations apply to its illustrated native-deproteinized-RNA implementation. The two reagent lanes retain separate Reaction, Reverse transcription and RNA hydrolysis instances; a shared caption does not imply pooling. The upper lane is interpreted as CMCT using the primary paper, while the lower lane is visibly DMS. Neither the unshown untreated control nor the related 2OMe-seq adaptation adds a depicted workflow target.
